# Histogram of Petal Length
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 0.5,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Iris Petal Length",
    x = "Petal Length (cm)",
    y = "Number of Observations"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
#Scatter Plot of Petal Length and Petal Width
```{r}
ggplot(
  iris,
  aes(
    x = Petal.Length,
    y = Petal.Width,
    color = Species
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Petal Length and Petal Width",
    x = "Petal Length (cm)",
    y = "Petal Width (cm)",
    color = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
#Box Plot of Petal Length by Species
```{r}
ggplot(
  iris,
  aes(
    x = Species,
    y = Petal.Length,
    fill = Species
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Petal Length by Iris Species",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Petal Length (cm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```
#Correlation Heatmap
```{r}
# Calculate the correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(iris[, 1:4])

# Convert the matrix to a data frame
cor_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_matrix))

# Create the heatmap
ggplot(
  cor_df,
  aes(
    x = Var1,
    y = Var2,
    fill = Freq
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Freq)),
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "firebrick",
    mid = "white",
    high = "steelblue",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Heatmap of Iris Measurements",
    x = "Measurement",
    y = "Measurement",
    fill = "Correlation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

```
#Species-Level Summary Statistics
```{r}
library(dplyr)

species_summary <- iris %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(
    Count = n(),
    Mean_Sepal_Length = mean(Sepal.Length),
    Mean_Sepal_Width = mean(Sepal.Width),
    Mean_Petal_Length = mean(Petal.Length),
    Mean_Petal_Width = mean(Petal.Width),
    SD_Petal_Length = sd(Petal.Length),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(species_summary)

```
#Correlation Calculation
```{r}
cor(
  iris[, 1:4],
  method = "pearson"
)

```
#Identifying Potential Outliers

```{r}
boxplot(

  col = "lightblue"
)

```
#COMPLETE R SCRIPT
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Load the dataset
data(iris)
df <- iris

# 2. Inspect the data
cat("Dataset dimensions:\n")
print(dim(df))

cat("\nColumn names:\n")
print(names(df))

cat("\nData structure:\n")
str(df)

cat("\nSummary statistics:\n")
print(summary(df))

# 3. Check data quality
cat("\nMissing values by column:\n")
print(colSums(is.na(df)))

cat("\nNumber of duplicated rows:\n")
print(sum(duplicated(df)))

cat("\nSpecies counts:\n")
print(table(df$Species))

# 4. Descriptive statistics
cat("\nMeans of numerical variables:\n")
print(sapply(df[, 1:4], mean))

cat("\nStandard deviations:\n")
print(sapply(df[, 1:4], sd))

# 5. Species-level summary
species_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(
    Count = n(),
    Mean_Sepal_Length = mean(Sepal.Length),
    Mean_Sepal_Width = mean(Sepal.Width),
    Mean_Petal_Length = mean(Petal.Length),
    Mean_Petal_Width = mean(Petal.Width),
    SD_Petal_Length = sd(Petal.Length),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(species_summary)

# 6. Calculate correlations
cor_matrix <- cor(df[, 1:4])

cat("\nCorrelation matrix:\n")
print(round(cor_matrix, 3))

# 7. Create an output folder
dir.create(
  "results",
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

# 8. Visualization 1: Histogram
p1 <- ggplot(
  df,
  aes(x = Petal.Length)
) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 0.5,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Iris Petal Length",
    x = "Petal Length (cm)",
    y = "Number of Observations"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p1)

ggsave(
  "results/figure1_histogram.png",
  plot = p1,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)

# 9. Visualization 2: Scatter plot
p2 <- ggplot(
  df,
  aes(
    x = Petal.Length,
    y = Petal.Width,
    color = Species
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    size = 3,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Petal Length and Petal Width by Species",
    x = "Petal Length (cm)",
    y = "Petal Width (cm)",
    color = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p2)

ggsave(
  "results/figure2_scatterplot.png",
  plot = p2,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)

# 10. Visualization 3: Box plot
p3 <- ggplot(
  df,
  aes(
    x = Species,
    y = Petal.Length,
    fill = Species
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Petal Length by Iris Species",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Petal Length (cm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  )

print(p3)

ggsave(
  "results/figure3_boxplot.png",
  plot = p3,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)

# 11. Visualization 4: Correlation heatmap
cor_df <- as.data.frame(
  as.table(cor_matrix)
)

p4 <- ggplot(
  cor_df,
  aes(
    x = Var1,
    y = Var2,
    fill = Freq
  )
) +
  geom_tile(
    color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Freq)),
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "firebrick",
    mid = "white",
    high = "steelblue",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Heatmap of Iris Measurements",
    x = "Measurement",
    y = "Measurement",
    fill = "Correlation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

print(p4)

ggsave(
  "results/figure4_correlation_heatmap.png",
  plot = p4,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

# 12. Export summary statistics
write.csv(
  species_summary,
  "results/species_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  cor_matrix,
  "results/correlation_matrix.csv"
)

cat(
  "\nAnalysis completed. Check the results folder ",
  "for the plots and summary files.\n",
  sep = ""
)

```
